record.one_liner: AI-powered search engine over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers that returns summaries, study metadata, citations and a Consensus Meter of supporting vs. refuting findings.
record.auth_notes: Per Consensus's llms-full.txt: the MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code with PKCE and dynamic client registration (recommended for multi-user agents). The REST API uses an API key sent as a bearer token, tied to an organization subscription. There is also an anonymous, heavily rate-limited MCP tier for evaluation. I could not fetch docs.consensus.app (403), so the key-issuance flow is unverified.
record.access_notes: Two routes. (1) MCP via OAuth: a Free account works (limited quota, 1 QPS, 10 papers per search by default), and an anonymous tier exists for evaluation. (2) REST API: the key is tied to an organization subscription. Which plan includes it, and whether it is self-serve, is not verified because docs.consensus.app returned 403 and the pricing page showed no plan details. I classed it paid_plan for REST on inference only. Treat it as unconfirmed. An unverified third-party guide gives the REST base URL as api.consensus.app/v1.
record.blocker: The API is read-only search (search, paper detail, synthesis, Consensus Meter), so it is narrow. The REST key needs an organization subscription, and the plan and self-serve status are unverified. MCP quotas are limited on the Free plan, and exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429. The official docs returned 403, so endpoint details are unconfirmed.
